reconstructed_theorem_text: Let I be a finite type with decidable equality, f:R^I->R any function, w in R^I with ||w||=1, u in R^I arbitrary, and a>=0 real. Let d=card(I), k be the real cast of the natural-number subtraction d-1, p_j(w)=e_j-w_j*w, sigma_j=sqrt(2*a)*p_j(w), and b=-u-a*k*w. Set Lf(w)=Laplacian(f)(w)-D(Df)(w)[w][w]-k*Df(w)[w]. Then Df(w)[b]+(1/2)*sum_j D(Df)(w)[sigma_j][sigma_j] = -Df(w)[u]+a*Lf(w). Here derivatives are the totalized Lean fderiv operators; the theorem makes no differentiability or smoothness assumption on f and no tangency assumption on u.
objects: I, f, unit vector w, arbitrary vector u, scalar a, dimension d, k=(d-1 in Nat) cast to R, projection-like vectors p_j, sigma_j, drift b, operator L.
domains: Finite EuclideanSpace R I; f real-valued; a real and nonnegative.
quantifiers: For every finite I, every f, every unit w, every u, and every nonnegative a, the displayed scalar identity holds.
assumptions: Decidable equality on I; ||w||=1; a>=0. No analytic regularity of f is assumed.
conclusion: Generator-form identity with the explicit second-derivative and radial correction operator L.
scopes: Pointwise algebraic identity at the given w; no time, probability, a.e., or limiting scope.
constant_dependencies: Only fixed coefficients 1/2 and 2 and dimension factor (card I-1) with natural subtraction. sigma,b,L depend exactly on the displayed inputs.
